header.regel: What is the HTML DOM?

keuzes.A: The DOM is the collection of variables created in JavaScript
keuzes.B: The DOM is short for Dominant Scripting and refers to JS higher functions
keuzes.C: The DOM is used to convert varibales from one type to another
keuzes.D: The Dom is a programming interface for web documents

vraag.uitleg:
The Document Object Model (DOM) is a programming interface for web documents. It represents the structure of an HTML document as a tree-like model, where each element in the document is represented by a node in the tree. The DOM provides a way to access, manipulate, and update the content and structure of web pages dynamically.
When a web page is loaded in a browser, the browser parses the HTML markup and creates a DOM tree that represents the structure of the page. The DOM tree consists of various types of nodes, such as elements, text nodes, attribute nodes, and more. Elements represent HTML tags, while text nodes contain the text content within elements.
JavaScript is a programming language commonly used in web development. It has a close relationship with the DOM because it provides powerful methods and properties to interact with the DOM tree. Using JavaScript, you can access and manipulate the DOM elements and their properties, change the content and appearance of the web page, and respond to user interactions. JavaScript can dynamically modify the DOM by adding, removing, or modifying elements and their attributes. You can use JavaScript to select elements by their tag names, class names, or IDs, and then manipulate their properties, such as changing their content, modifying their styles, or attaching event handlers.

It provides a command-line interface where you can execute JavaScript code, view and modify the Document Object Model (DOM), inspect network requests and responses, log messages for debugging purposes, and access various other tools and features for web development.

header.regel: Which of the following best describes an array in JavaScript?

header.regel: Which of the following best describes type coercion in JavaScript?

vraag.uitleg:
Type coercion in JavaScript refers to the process of converting one data type to another automatically and implicitly by the JavaScript engine when performing operations that involve different data types. JavaScript is a dynamically typed language, which means that variables can hold values of any data type, and type checking is done at runtime.
When you perform operations involving different data types (e.g., addition, comparison, etc.), JavaScript will try to convert one or both of the operands to a common data type to make the operation meaningful. This automatic conversion is what we call type coercion.

header.regel: What are the differences between 'var', 'let', and 'const' in JavaScript?

header.regel: What is the difference between '==' and '===' in JavaScript?

vraag.uitleg: A higher-order function is a function that takes another function as an argument or returns a function as its result. It treats functions as values and allows for the composition of functions and the creation of more abstract and reusable code.

header.regel: What is prototypal inheritance in JavaScript?

keuzes.D: Prototypal inheritance is a method to create dynamic HTML elements using JavaScript.

vraag.uitleg: Prototypal inheritance is a mechanism in JavaScript where objects can inherit properties and methods from other objects. It allows objects to be based on other objects, which can serve as prototypes. When a property or method is accessed on an object, if it is not found on the object itself, JavaScript looks up the prototype chain until it finds the property or method.

header.regel: What are promises in JavaScript?

keuzes.A: Promises are a way to handle errors in JavaScript.
keuzes.B: Promises are a technique for making asynchronous HTTP requests to the server from JavaScript.

vraag.uitleg: Promises are objects used for handling and chaining asynchronous operations in JavaScript. They represent the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation and allow you to attach callbacks to be executed when the operation is successful (resolved) or encounters an error (rejected). Promises help simplify asynchronous programming and provide a more readable and structured way to handle async operations.

header.regel: How do you handle errors in JavaScript?

vraag.uitleg: Errors in JavaScript can be handled using try-catch statements. The code that may potentially throw an error is placed inside a 'try' block, and if an error occurs, it is caught and handled in the 'catch' block. This allows you to gracefully handle errors, log them, or perform alternative actions when something goes wrong in your code.

header.regel: What is the difference between dot notation and bracket notation for accessing object properties in JavaScript?

keuzes.A: There is no difference; dot notation and bracket notation can be used interchangeably.

The 'map' method, on the other hand, also iterates over each element of an array but returns a new array containing the results of applying a function to each element. It does not modify the original array.
